text: {"lessons":["I sold several winners in fixed 25-share amounts, while holding Stock B until a very large loss. I should not let the pleasure of realizing gains or the pain of realizing losses dictate when I sell; decisions should follow a consistent plan based on current prospects and risk.","Selling Stock A and Stock B at losses did not make those sales mistakes, just as earlier gains did not prove my timing was good. I should judge each decision by the information available then, not by my purchase price or the outcome alone.","After selling Stock E, I bought it again at higher prices, and I also added to Stock C. Before each purchase, I should reassess the investment case, position size, and portfolio-wide exposure rather than trade from habit or a desire to recover prior results."]}
